taglines: It is Monday morning and you have already made three micro-decisions before checking a single email and each micro-decision felt small and irrelevant in the moment and you will not remember any of them but somewhere in your body they are tallied and the tally is what Monday feels like by 11am.

The weekend happened. You have forensic evidence of this. Dishes. A receipt. A notification from an app that tracked how many steps you did not take on Saturday. The weekend has been processed and filed and Monday has resumed without explanation and without apology.

Somewhere right now a project manager is writing 'per my last email' and choosing not to send it and writing 'just following up' instead and both of them know what was meant and neither of them will say it and this is called professional communication.

You are entering week twenty-five of the year. Week twenty-five has not done anything to you personally but you are looking at it with a kind of exhausted suspicion that is probably its fault and probably yours and honestly probably both.

Your coffee is the right temperature for exactly a seventeen-second window and you were doing something else during those seventeen seconds and you know this and you are not going to do anything about it and you are going to drink the coffee anyway and you are going to call this acceptance.

Monday has a reputation and the reputation is earned but it is also somewhat unfair because Monday is just doing its job which is being the first day and the first day of anything has a structural disadvantage and if you think about it Monday is kind of heroic but you are not going to think about it.

You have a meeting at ten that could have been an email and an email thread that should have been a meeting and somewhere in the space between those two facts is where your entire morning went. The space does not have a name. On your calendar it says 'focus time.'

June 22nd. Eight days until the month ends. The month that you were going to use to finally get ahead of things is now a month that you are going to finish at roughly the same velocity at which you started it and there is a certain consistency to this that if you squint looks like character.
